card.name: Words linking cause and adverse event
card.fires_on: Words in warning text that link a cause to an outcome, such as "were" after events, "-related" after treatment, or "following" after patients. It also fires on cause-related word parts such as "caus" and "conf".

modes.label: Cause-link words
modes.description: Short linking words or word parts that tie a therapy or event to a harm or diagnosis.
modes.example: Instances of nasal septum perforation occurred in patients<< following>> the nasal application of corticosteroids

modes.label: Inside disease terms
modes.description: The end of a condition name or word partway through, after a cause phrase.
modes.example: may be associated with an increased risk of Clostridium difficile associated<< diarrhea>>, especially in hospitalized patients.

card.writes: It pushes against words meaning "thanks to" or "depends on" (mostly Chinese terms), so there is no clear output effect for English medical text.
card.plain: It marks the small words in a warning that connect a drug or event to a bad outcome.
